claim_tested: gp15 is an active cell-wall-degrading lysozyme-like enzyme
key_finding: Purified phi29 gene 15 product lyses Bacillus subtilis cell walls with activity comparable to T4 gene e and P22 gene 19 products
context: phi29 gene 15 expressed and purified; B. subtilis cell-wall lysis assay
confidence: high for activity, none for bond chemistry
limitation: Turbidimetric/lysis readout does not identify the cleaved product, so it cannot distinguish hydrolysis (EC 3.2.1.17) from a lytic transglycosylase reaction (EC 4.2.2.n2)

claim_tested: The GH24 second carboxylate (T4L Asp20) is required for catalysis
key_finding: T4 lysozyme D20C retains close to wild-type specific activity with an unchanged pH-activity profile
context: Bacteriophage T4 lysozyme, purified protein, in vitro
limitation: T4L is a different GH24 subfamily; does not prove a gp15-type enzyme is active

claim_tested: Which carboxylate is the essential catalytic residue in GH24
key_finding: Glu11 is required as the general acid; Asp20 is not essential for activity
context: Bacteriophage T4 lysozyme, purified protein, in vitro

claim_tested: A single-carboxylate GH24 endolysin hydrolyses the glycosidic bond
key_finding: Phage lambda endolysin R is a transglycosylase forming a 1,6-anhydro-MurNAc product, not a hydrolase
context: Phage lambda R protein, purified, on E. coli murein sacculi
limitation: Lambda R is the GH24 member most similar in active-site composition to gp15, but it is not a direct gp15 measurement

claim_tested: A GH24 active site with one carboxylate can be catalytically complete
key_finding: No acidic side chain within 8 A of the Glu19 carboxylate; nearest contacts Ser126 3.53 A, Ala125 4.11 A, Gln68 4.72 A, Tyr67 4.97 A, Ser18 5.14 A
context: Crystal structure of lambda lysozyme, chain A; distances computed from coordinates

claim_tested: Where the Asp20 carboxylate sits relative to the scissile bond
key_finding: In the 148L T26E covalent intermediate (LINK Glu26 OE2 to MurNAc C1, 1.51 A), Asp20 OD2 is 4.09 A and Glu11 OE1 4.20 A from C1; in wild-type 2LZM superposed on 148L (162 CA, RMSD 0.57 A) Asp20 OD1 is 3.61 A and Glu11 OE2 3.86 A from C1
context: T4 lysozyme with bound peptidoglycan fragment
limitation: Defines the Asp20 volume in T4L numbering only; transfer to gp15 is by alignment, not by an experimental gp15 structure

claim_tested: Another acidic or polar residue occupies the Asp20 volume in the gp15 active-site cleft
key_finding: In the closest experimental template to gp15 (PHAb10 GH24 domain, 1.52 A, 47.9% identity over 142 residues) only three acidic side chains lie within 10 A of the catalytic Glu37: Glu37 (0.60 A), Asp84 (8.33 A) and Asp46 (8.61 A); their gp15 equivalents are Glu15, Asp60 and Pro26. Across the whole 26-residue active-site shell gp15 introduces no new acidic residue
context: Experimental crystal structure used as template because no gp15 structure or AlphaFold model exists
limitation: Template-based inference, 47.9% identity; side-chain rotamers in gp15 itself are unknown

claim_tested: A compensating acidic residue appears at the Asp20 position across phage GH24 homologs lacking the Asp
key_finding: 0/45 phi29-like and c2-like endolysins carry Asp or Glu at the T4L Asp20 column (Pro 41, Val 3, Lys 1) versus 9/23 reviewed non-clade GH24 entries, Fisher exact p = 1.66e-05. The Glu11 column is Glu 37/37 and the Thr26 column is Thr 45/45. gp15 Asp41 occurs only in the Bacillus subgroup (8 Asp, 2 Glu, 3 Val) and is absent from all 32 Lactococcus members
context: UniProt PF00959 entries from Salasmaviridae, Ceduovirus, Picovirinae; Gotoh BLOSUM62 alignment to P11187
confidence: high for the column assignment at the Thr26/His31 anchor, medium for the exact slot within the 2-residue clade insertion
limitation: Alignment-based; the insertion at gp15 24-25 means the Asp20 slot could be Ala24, Val25 or Pro26, none of which is acidic, so the conclusion is unchanged

claim_tested: c2-like lysins, the closest characterised gp15 relatives, are muramidases
key_finding: A muramidase motif was found in the lysins of c2-like phages
limitation: Motif-based assignment with no product determination, so it cannot discriminate hydrolase from lytic transglycosylase

claim_tested: Superpose the gp15 AlphaFold model onto T4 lysozyme bound to peptidoglycan
key_finding: No AlphaFold model exists for P11187 or for any of the GH24 viral proteins checked (P07540, Q37896, P62692, P62693, P00720, P03706, P09963); AFDB returns HTTP 404 because viral proteomes are excluded. The ESMFold public API returned HTTP 504. The prescribed superposition could not be run as written
context: alphafold.ebi.ac.uk API and files endpoint; api.esmatlas.com
limitation: Substituted the 47.9%-identity experimental structure 9KBQ as the structural proxy; this is stated as a deviation from the prescribed analysis
